question: Which Constitutional Amendment reduced the voting age from 21 years to 18 years in India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sixty-first Amendment Act, 1988**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The **Sixty-first Amendment Act of 1988** reduced the **voting age** for elections to the Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assemblies from **21 years to 18 years**.
 
• This amendment aimed to enhance political participation by empowering the youth of India to take part in the electoral process.
 
• The amendment modified **Article 326** of the Constitution of India, which deals with elections to the House of the People and Legislative Assemblies of States based on adult suffrage. *Hence, the statement is correct.*
 
• The reduction in voting age was considered essential for increasing democratic participation and ensuring that more citizens, especially the younger population, can actively contribute to decision-making in governance.
